record.original_question: Does every Seidel matrix with exactly three distinct rational eigenvalues contain a regular graph in its switching class?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.34. Does every Seidel matrix with precisely three distinct rational eigenvalues contain a regular graph in its switching class ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Seidel matrix of order n is a symmetric n×n matrix S with zero diagonal and off-diagonal entries in {−1, +1}. Equivalently, given a simple graph G on vertex set {1,…,n}, its Seidel matrix S(G) has entries S_{ij} = −1 if ij is an edge of G, S_{ij} = +1 if i ≠ j and ij is a non-edge, and S_{ii} = 0. Two graphs G and G' on the same vertex set are said to be Seidel-switching equivalent if there exists a subset U of the vertex set such that G' is obtained from G by complementing all edges between U and its complement (and leaving the edges inside U and inside its complement unchanged); the equivalence class of G under this relation is called its switching class. Equivalently, S(G') = D S(G) D for some diagonal ±1 matrix D, so all Seidel matrices in one switching class share the same spectrum. A Seidel matrix S is said to "contain a regular graph in its switching class" if there exists a graph G' in the switching class such that G' is a regular graph.

Question: Does every Seidel matrix whose spectrum consists of exactly three distinct eigenvalues, all of which are rational numbers, contain a regular graph in its switching class?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. Related work shows that every Seidel matrix of order at most 12 with exactly three distinct eigenvalues has a regular graph in its switching class, and the same holds for all Seidel matrices of odd order with three distinct eigenvalues. However, examples of Seidel matrices of order ≥14 with three distinct (irrational) eigenvalues exist whose switching class contains no regular graph. The rational-eigenvalue case specifically does not appear to have been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Equiangular line systems and switching classes containing regular graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies when a Seidel matrix with three distinct eigenvalues has a regular graph in its switching class; proves results for small orders and odd orders, and produces counterexamples for some orders ≥14.
status_evidence.claim: The general three-eigenvalue version is not always true, but partial results and the rational-eigenvalue restriction remain investigated.

status_evidence.title: Maximality of Seidel matrices and switching roots of graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Further investigation of switching roots and Seidel matrices with three eigenvalues.
status_evidence.claim: Continued research indicates the rational case is not yet settled.
